body:
A customer reported to us an issue with their spine-godot mono project; after some extensive investigation, I can reproduce the same underlying failure with a small C# MRP.

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in official Godot `4.7.1.stable.mono.official.a13da4feb`.
- Reproducible in official Godot `4.8.dev2.mono.official.7220d456d`, the latest available development Mono build at the time of this test.
- Host: Windows, .NET runtime 8.0.27.

The MRP creates `Node` signal sources and short-lived `Resource` signal targets. It drops the managed target references, starts garbage collection without waiting for finalizers, and queues the sources for deletion on the main thread.

### Reproduction

```text
Godot_v4.8-dev2_mono_win64_console.exe --headless --path GodotSignalRace --verbose -- -SourcesPerFrame=1 -TargetsPerSource=32 -GcEveryFrames=1 -MaxFps=60 -DurationSeconds=10 -EmitBeforeDelete=false -QuitAfterFirstGc=false
```

Do not add `GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers()`, because that blocks the main thread and removes the concurrency that this MRP tests.

### Result

Both official builds crashed in approximately five seconds with exit status 5.

Godot 4.8 dev2 failed after the last progress report showed 59 frames and 1,888 targets. The failure was:

```text
Fatal error. System.AccessViolationException: Attempted to read or write protected memory.
   at Godot.NativeInterop.NativeFuncs.godotsharp_internal_refcounted_disposed(...)
   at Godot.GodotObject.Dispose(Boolean)
   at Godot.GodotObject.Finalize()
```

Godot 4.7.1 failed through the same stack after the last progress report showed 121 frames and 3,872 targets.

This appears to occur because `GodotObject.Finalize()` calls `Dispose(false)` on the CLR finalizer thread. For a managed wrapper around a `RefCounted`, that call can release the final native reference and run native object and signal teardown concurrently with main-thread source deletion.

As supporting evidence, I also performed a controlled test with Godot 4.5.1. The stock official executable and `GodotSharp.dll` reproduced the crash. The same native executable stopped reproducing it when only finalizer-origin managed disposal was moved to the main thread. A 4.5.1 backport of #117511 alone still reproduced the failure.

I have attached the MRP and concise summaries containing the exact commands, binary hashes, and results.

> AI disclosure: I used ChatGPT to help organize the test evidence and review candidate designs. I personally reproduced the issue, built the MRP, and verified the reported results.
